title: Coral and the Radiators
premise: Edmund 'Edie' Delacroix has tuned the pianos of the Verrone house for fifteen years, listening to its radiators tick out the rhythms of a family she never quite joined—and never quite left. When a late-night radio broadcast airs a song only one person ever wrote, her long-dead mentor's unfinished lullaby, Edie realizes someone in that house has been keeping more than silence. Returning to the old neighborhood before the last bus route is rerouted forever, she must confront the night she almost spoke and didn't, claim the inheritance no will ever named, and finally play the song aloud—ending not with belonging granted but with belonging claimed.
about_author: Ivo Pemberton is the pen name of a former piano tuner's apprentice who spent a decade in coastal mill towns collecting the stories houses tell through their pipes. This is their second novel, written mostly on night buses.

chapters.title: The Tuning Fork Year
chapters.summary: Edie, POV first person, introduces her ritual: tuning the Verrone grand every third Thursday while the radiators clank their private history. She catalogs what she hears—arguments, births, a death—but says nothing. Emotional beat: comfortable invisibility beginning to itch.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Almost
chapters.summary: Flashback to nineteen-year-old Edie arriving as apprentice to Auguste Verrone, the composer who taught her to hear buildings. Whose POV: Edie. She recalls the night she overheard something she was never meant to hear and chose silence. Beat: guilt established as her native language.

chapters.title: Static on the Late Shift
chapters.summary: Present day: insomniac Edie hears a radio performance of a melody she knows was written and never recorded—Auguste's lullaby for his daughter Coral. POV Edie. The announcer credits it to a living composer. Beat: the floor drops; invisibility was a choice someone else also made.

chapters.title: Coral, Age Nine
chapters.summary: Second flashback: young Coral Verrone, POV hers, adoring the quiet tuner who fixed her father's piano and let her press one key. She remembers Edie leaving abruptly one autumn. Beat: we learn Edie mattered to someone who noticed her absence.

chapters.title: The Last Bus Notice
chapters.summary: Edie learns the 42 route through the old neighborhood is being permanently rerouted next month—a bureaucratic erasure of her entire past geography. POV Edie, with her landlady Marta as foil. Beat: deadline pressure converts dread into motion.

chapters.title: What the Radiators Keep
chapters.summary: Edie returns to the Verrone house under pretense of a final tuning. The radiators sound wrong—grief has a pitch, she realizes. Coral, now thirty, answers the door. POV alternates via Edie's observation. Beat: two silences meet and recognize each other.

chapters.title: Tea with the Ghost's Daughter
chapters.summary: Coral hires Edie for a full restoration, oddly formal, oddly urgent. Over tea they circle the past like cats. POV Edie. Coral mentions the radio premiere casually; Edie doesn't reveal she knows. Beat: mutual withholding, tension braided.

chapters.title: Auguste's Last Winter
chapters.summary: Flashback to the composer's final months: he asked Edie to help him finish the lullaby and record it; she refused, terrified of overstepping. He died with it unrecorded. POV Edie. Beat: her central wound exposed—the refusal that became a life.

chapters.title: The Locked Music Room
chapters.summary: Restoration work leads Edie to Auguste's sealed music room; Coral claims she lost the key years ago. Edie hears, through the radiator behind that wall, a rhythm unlike grief—deliberate, recent. POV Edie. Beat: mystery sharpens into suspicion.

chapters.title: Uncle Theo's Chords
chapters.summary: Theo, Auguste's brother and executor, appears—charming, proprietary. He claims credit arrangements for the radio piece. POV shifts to Coral watching Theo handle her father's legacy like furniture. Beat: antagonist revealed; inheritance as theft.

chapters.title: A Song Is Not a Object
chapters.summary: Coral confronts Theo privately; he insists Auguste gave him the lullaby before dying. Coral half-believes him. POV Coral. Her doubt curdles toward Edie too—who did the tuner really serve? Beat: alliance fractures before it forms.

chapters.title: The Rhythm Behind the Wall
chapters.summary: Night visit: Edie confirms someone has been playing the piano in the locked room—someone alive, practicing the lullaby badly. She finds fresh rosin dust. POV Edie. Beat: the house itself becomes witness; dread turns investigative.

chapters.title: Marta's Bus Map
chapters.summary: Back home, Edie spreads old route maps with Marta and admits, aloud, everything. First time she has said any of it. POV Edie. Marta tells her about her own unsaid life. Beat: confession as rehearsal; found family foreshadowed.

chapters.title: The Apprentice Nobody Hired
chapters.summary: Flashback: how Auguste actually took Edie in after her mother's eviction—not charity but recognition; he heard her hum his unpublished étude from the street. POV Edie. Beat: belonging once offered and squandered; stakes become personal debt.

chapters.title: Key Under the Third Valve
chapters.summary: Following radiator logic, Edie finds the music room key hidden where Auguste hid everything—in the boiler room, taped inside valve three, with a note bearing her name. POV Edie. Beat: the dead man's message lands like a hand on the shoulder.

chapters.title: What the Note Said
chapters.summary: The note: 'For whoever hears the house finish my sentence.' Inside the room, Edie finds the lullaby manuscript—dated after Auguste's death, in Coral's handwriting. POV Edie, stunned. Beat: revelation reframes everything; Coral is the composer.

chapters.title: Coral's Confession
chapters.summary: Confronted gently, Coral breaks: she reconstructed her father's fragment from memory and recorded it herself, letting Theo broker it, unable to admit authorship in a house that worshipped him. POV Coral. Beat: mirror image—two people who practiced almost-saying-it.

chapters.title: Theo's Ledger
chapters.summary: Edie and Coral discover Theo has been siphoning royalties and plans to sell the house before the bus reroute kills its value. POV alternating. They realize only proof of Coral's authorship can stop both sale and theft. Beat: rising action peaks; clock ticking.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Reroute
chapters.summary: Final night of the 42 route. Edie retrieves Auguste's original sketchbook from a depot storage locker using the key and a tuner's credentials. Theo intercepts her; a raw confrontation where she finally says the thing she withheld at nineteen. POV Edie. Beat: climax of voice.

chapters.title: Last Bus Home
chapters.summary: On the final 42 ride, passengers who share the neighborhood's history ride together—strangers becoming chorus. Edie carries the sketchbook; Coral waits at the terminus. POV Coral. Beat: communal catharsis; the city itself testifies.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.summary: In the unlocked music room, Coral plays the finished lullaby while Edie tunes the piano live around her—correction and creation together. They record it properly, both names on the label. Theo's fraud collapses under dated manuscripts. POV Edie. Beat: resolution of craft and truth.

chapters.title: Radiators, Warm
chapters.summary: Months later: Edie keeps a key to the Verrone house, teaches Coral's daughter to hear the pipes, and the rerouted bus line gets a stop renamed for Auguste. Belonging, she understands now, is tuned, not given. POV Edie. Final beat: the house's history continues, and she is inside it.
